sentences.text:
This is an application for pre-arrest bail in connection with CR No.210 of 2023 registered with Vishrambag Police Station, Pune City, for the offences punishable under Sections 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("the Penal Code") and Section 3 of the Maharashtra 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act,
1999.
3.

entities.text:
Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act,
1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Mangesh Khare (the first informant) and the applicants reside in the same apartment at Pune.
The applicants were operating Shriram Gas Agency, a LPG Distributorship of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd. ("BPCL").

The applicants allegedly made a representation to the first informant that if the money was invested in the business of the said Gas Agency, the first informant would get lucrative returns far in excess of the Bank deposit.
The first informant was thus induced to transfer an amount of Rs.14,10,000/- in the accounts of applicant No.1 Uday Joshi and Shriram Gas Agency.
The applicants had also represented that, they had the authority to accept the deposits from the public and issue fixed deposit receipts.
The applicants committed default in repayment of the said amount and the return thereon.
When the first informant insisted for repayment of the amount, he was threatened with dire consequences.
4. It further transpired that the applicants had also deceived other eight investors named in the FIR in a similar fashion.
The total defrauded amount was to the tune of Rs.5,53,8000/-.
The applicants had issued the fixed deposit 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC receipts without any authorization from Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
Having realized the fraud, the first informant lodged the report.

5. When the application was listed before the Court on 10th November, 2023, this Court was persuaded to grant interim protection as time was sought on behalf of the prosecution and the first informant-intervener and it was also submitted that out of the alleged defrauded amount of Rs.5,53,8000/-, the applicants had repaid more than Rs.4 Crores and one of the alleged investors,
Mr. Mayuresh Zore had addressed a letter to the Investigating Officer to the effect that the said investor had no grievance against the applicants.
6. Harshad Deshpande, one of the investors, has filed IA/4495/2023, opposing the prayer of pre-arrest bail.

The first informant has filed IA/4506/2023.
7.
The applicants have filed an affidavit-in-reply in response to the interim application.
8. An additional affidavit in support of the application came to be filed by the applicant.

As certain statements have been made in the additional affidavit regarding repayment of 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC the amount by the applicants, an additional affidavit has also been filed on behalf of the interveners controverting the claim of repayment.

9. Perused the material on record, including the FIR and the documents relied upon by the applicants and the interveners.
10.
Heard Mr. Samir Vaidya, the learned Counsel for the applicants, Smt. Ganapathy, the learned APP for the State and Mr. Mundargi, the learned Counsel for the intervener, at some length.

2 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Vaidya, the learned Counsel for the applicants, submitted that the applicants had appeared in response to the notice under Section 41A(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Post interim order passed by this Court, the applicants appeared before the Investigating Officer and have rendered necessary co-operation.
Thus, at this stage, the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not at all warranted.
In any event, according to Mr. Vaidya, the material on record indicates that a substantial amount has been repaid to the persons, who had lent money to the applicants.
Thus, the offence punishable under Section 3 of the MPID Act, is not at all attracted.

Laying emphasis on the 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC fact that one of the investors Mr. Mayuresh Zore,
who had allegedly lent a sum of Rs.2.25 Crores, has stated that he has no grievance against the applicants, Mr. Vaidya would urge that the applicants have been roped in with an oblique motive to take control of Shriram Gas Agency.

Attention of the Court was invited to the documents annexed to the additional affidavit to lend support to the submission that a substantial part of the amount has been repaid to the alleged investors.

Thus, the arrest and detention of the applicants would be detrimental to the interest of the investors to whom the applicants are still repaying the amount,
submitted Mr. Vaidya.
12. In opposition to this, Smt. Ganapathy, the learned APP, stoutly resisted the prayer for pre-arrest bail.
It was submitted that each of the investors, who has been defrauded by the applicants, has stated during the course of investigation about the manner in which the applicants defrauded them.

Though the applicants have placed the copies of the purported statements of accounts to substantiate the claim that they have repaid a substantial amount to the investors yet, before the Investigating Officer, a stand was taken that they were not in custody of the 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC statements of account.
The claim of repayment is contentious.

At any rate, according to Mr.
Ganapathy, since the applicants have issued fixed deposit receipts falsely claiming that they were authorized to accept the fixed deposit from public and issue the deposit receipts and BPCL has categorically informed that it had never issued any authorization to the applicant for issuing the fixed deposit receipts, custodial interrogation of the applicants is warranted to unearth the fraud and the circumstances in which such fixed deposit receipts came to be issued.
13. Mr. Mundargi, the learned Counsel for the interveners, submitted that the claim of the applicants that they have repaid a substantial amount is demonstrably false.
In the additional affidavit on behalf of the interveners, the exact amount which has been repaid alongwith the statements of accounts was sought to be brought on record.

Mr. Mundargi further submitted that the applicants have attempted to wriggle out of the situation by belatedly taking a defence in the affidavit-in-reply, that their signatures were obtained on blank letterheads of Shriram Gas Agency by the Advocate, who represented the informant party in the proceedings before the Court.
It was further submitted that the 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC applicants have also resorted to intimidation of the investors and reports have been lodged with the police.
Therefore, the applicants do not deserve the discretionary relief of pre-arrest bail.
14. I have given anxious consideration to the aforesaid submissions.
First and foremost, the fact that the applicants had accepted deposits from the first informant and other investors is not seriously put in contest.
The thrust of the submission of Mr. Vaidya was that a major part of the amount was repaid.

From the perusal of the statement of the witnesses recorded during the course of Uday Trimbak Joshi vs State Of Maharashtra on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151486583/
3 investigation, it appears that some part of the amount invested by few of the witnesses was repaid.

entities.text: Uday Trimbak Joshi vs State Of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Few of the witnesses
have stated that no part of the amount invested by them has been repaid.
In any event, the aspect of repayment is rooted in the facts.
The applicants do not claim that they have repaid the entire amount of all the investors.
The submission was that there was no intent to defraud the investors.
15. At this stage, it is necessary to note that there are more than 11 victims.
Prima facie an element of system, continuity and repetition in the dealings of the applicants becomes evident.
What exacerbates the situation is the issue of fixed 6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC deposit receipts.
The applicants had issued fixed deposit receipts claiming that they were authorized to accept the deposits from the public and issue deposit receipts as per RBI/SEBI guidelines.

One of such receipts was issued to Mr. Harshad Deshpande, the intervener in IA/4495/2023, from whom an amount of Rs.91,91,768/- was accepted with a promise that the said amount would be repaid within a period of 12 months with interest at the rate of 2.5% per month.
Similar receipts appear to have been issued to Jayashri Khare and Mangesh Khare promising to repay the amounts within six months with interest at the rate of 12% p.a..
As noted above, BPCL has clarified that it had never authorized Shriram Gas Agency to accept such deposits.

16. Mr. Viadya attempted to salvage the position by asserting that the circumstances in which the applicants were coerced to be sign blank letter heads of Shriram Gas Agency have been explained in the affidavit-in-reply to the intervention application.
Therefore, the issue of fixed deposit receipts cannot be said to be such an incriminating circumstance as to warrant the custodial interrogation of the applicants.
I find it rather difficult to accede to aforesaid submission.

It is imperative to note that in the FIR itself Mangesh Khare had alleged that the applicants issued fixed deposit receipts without any authorization from RBI and thereby induced them to invest the amount.

It does not appear that in the application for pre-arrest bail either before the Court of Session or this Court, the applicants made an endeavour to offer the explanation, which was sought to be offered when the interveners placed on record the copies of the fixed deposit receipts.
This factor assumes critical salience.
I thus find substance in the submission of Mr. Mundargi that the applicants have belatedly offered an explanation implicating the Advocate for the interveners to wriggle out of the situation.
18. The fact that the applicants were not authorized to accept the deposits from public and issue the fixed deposit receipts is beyond cavil.
Therefore, the investigation is warranted regarding the circumstances in which the fixed deposit receipts were issued and the investors were thereby induced to part with the amount.

Custodial interrogation of the applicants is, therefore,
indispensable.

4 19.

entities.text: ABA3245-2023+.DOC Uday Trimbak Joshi vs State Of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission of Mr. Vaidya that one of the major investors has claimed that he has no grievance against the applicants, is required to be appreciated in the light of the material on record which indicates that two NC reports were lodged by two of the investors to the effect that the applicants, and other persons, at the behest of the applicants, threatened them with dire consequences, if the cases against the applicants were not withdrawn.
I have perused the letter addressed by Mayuresh Zore.
Pertinently, Mayuresh Zore did not dispute that there were financial transactions between him and Mayuresh Joshi - the applicant No.2.
However, he claimed that he has no grievance against the applicants.

If viewed in the backdrop of the reports lodged by two other investors regarding the threats by the applicants, the submission on behalf of the prosecution that there has been an attempt to tamper with evidence and threaten the witnesses cannot be said to be unfounded.

20. In the totality of the circumstances, in my view, custodial interrogation of the applicants is warranted to facilitate further investigation, unearth the fraud in all its facets, unmask the identity of other persons who were involved in the fraud, and also have the money trail.

I am,
6-ABA3245-2023+.DOC therefore, not inclined to grant pre-arrest bail to the applicants.
21.

Hence, the following order:
:ORDER:
(i) Application stands rejected.
(ii) It is clarified that these prima facie observations are confined to determine entitlement to pre-arrest bail only.
Application disposed.
In view of disposal of ABA/3245/2023, interim applications stand disposed.

[N. J. JAMADAR, J.]
